purpose: LLM comparison for content creation, SEO, and site development tasks

tasks.taskName: SEO Tasks (Titles, Metas, On-Page Optimization, Structured Data)
tasks.description: Rewriting titles, meta descriptions, H1s, introductions, adding emotional language while keeping facts accurate, improving scannability and schema.

my_recommendation.reason: Most precise with HTML/schema, follows strict length and format rules, rarely hallucinates facts.
my_recommendation.notes: Grok is too inconsistent with structured data formatting.

tasks.description: Writing full new book vs movie comparison articles from scratch, including research synthesis, balanced analysis, and structured sections.

my_recommendation.reason: Superior long-form reasoning, maintains honest/spoiler-heavy tone naturally, best verdict sections.
my_recommendation.notes: Grok is fine for short or opinion-heavy pieces but lacks depth for 2000+ word comparisons.

tasks.description: Large-scale HTML editing, homepage improvements, adding hero sections, cards, internal linking, and preserving existing CSS/schema.

my_recommendation.reason: Handles long context windows best, preserves untouched code reliably, precise surgical edits.
my_recommendation.notes: Grok is faster for small iterative tweaks but messes up existing structure on large files.

tasks.description: Creating todo lists, reviewing GSC data, prioritizing fixes, refining automation prompts, and overall site strategy.

my_recommendation.reason: Best at strategic synthesis, connects GSC data to actionable plans without overcomplicating.
my_recommendation.notes: Grok wins here — faster, less cautious, more direct.

tasks.description: Designing landing pages, hero sections, card layouts, navigation, and improving user flow.

my_recommendation.reason: Very fast HTML/CSS prototyping, good at user-first layout suggestions.
my_recommendation.notes: Claude is more polished but slower; Grok wins for iteration speed.

tasks.description: Finding current trends, upcoming adaptations, or verifying details for new pages.

my_recommendation.reason: Best real-time search with citations, ideal for upcoming book-to-movie adaptations and release dates.
my_recommendation.notes: Grok has live knowledge but less reliable citations than Perplexity.

general_guidelines.tone: Honest, spoiler-heavy, no sugarcoating, opinionated but factual
general_guidelines.site_strength: Deep individual comparison pages with structured data and verdicts
general_guidelines.current_focus: Improving CTR on existing impressions and making homepage more welcoming
general_guidelines.recommended_workflow: Claude for heavy editing and writing → Grok for strategy and quick tests → Perplexity for timely research

responses.seo_optimization: Good for brainstorming, weak for final schema.
responses.html_refactoring: Fast but error-prone on large files.

llm_comparison_results.overall_notes: Best for strategy, UX iteration, and quick drafts. Not for production SEO or structured data.

responses.new_content_creation: Best in class for long-form comparisons.
responses.html_refactoring: Superior context handling and surgical edits.

llm_comparison_results.overall_notes: Workhorse for production content and technical SEO. Use for final deliverables.

responses.research_timely: Best for citations and real-time adaptation news.

llm_comparison_results.overall_notes: Use only for research layer, not content generation.
